messages.content: Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
I shall be a wife.

PIE: pótnih₂ h₁ésoh₂.
Gloss: mistress-NOM.SG be-SBJV.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The wolf comes in the night; the shepherd stays awake. The man who steals eats and is not satisfied.

PIE: wĺ̥kʷos kʷsépi gʷm̥yéti poh₂imḗn bʰéwdʰeti. stéh₂yonts h₂nḗr h₁ḗdti ne-kʷe tetórpe.
Gloss: wolf-NOM.SG night-LOC.SG come-PRS.3SG shepherd-NOM.SG be.awake-PRS.3SG steal-PTCP.ACT.NOM.SG man-NOM.SG eat-PRS.3SG NEG=and be.satisfied-PRF.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu só h₃rḗǵs sékʷt.

English: The king said:
Gloss: NU demonstrative_so-NOM.SG king-NOM.SG say-AOR.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
In distress the dear one is known. Do not deceive your dear one.

PIE: lewbʰós h₂égʰesi ǵn̥nh₃tór. wíHre lewbʰóm mē dʰrugʰyés.
Gloss: dear-NOM.SG distress-LOC.SG know-MID.PRS.3SG man-VOC.SG dear-ACC.SG NEG deceive-INJ.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The great Sun.

PIE: méǵh₂ sóh₂wl̥.
Gloss: big-ACC.SG sun-ACC.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Whoever wears that wool, the shepherd kills.

PIE: h₁yós tā́m h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m wéstor poh₂imḗn tóm moréyeti.
Gloss: relative_yo-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG wool-ACC.SG be.wearing-MID.PRS.3SG shepherd-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG kill-PRS.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₁nómn̥ moy wĺ̥kʷos h₁ésti. ph₂tḗr moy dl̥h₁gʰósyo gʰóstis h₁ést.

English: My name is Wolf. My father was the guest of the Long One.
Gloss: name-NOM.SG personal/1-DAT.SG.ENCL wolf-NOM.SG be-PRS.3SG father-NOM.SG personal/1-GEN.SG.ENCL long-GEN.SG guest-NOM.SG be-PST.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu diwéy HréwdHt.

English: Sweating, he grew tired.
Gloss: NU sky-DAT.SG cry.(vocally)-PST.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu moy h₁éḱwos h₁ésti.

English: The stallion is mine.
Gloss: NU personal/1-DAT.SG.ENCL stallion-NOM.SG be-PRS.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
tósyo mḗms lelóykʷe só-kʷe tósmōd déh₂nus léytt.

English: Its meat is gone, and it went away from the river.
Gloss: demonstrative_so-GEN.SG flesh-NOM.SG be.missing-PRF.3SG demonstrative_so-NOM.SG=and demonstrative_so-ABL.SG river-ABL.SG go.(away)-AOR.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
If I lie to you, may the gods strike me down. Give me my wage.

PIE: h₁yód te dʰrugʰyṓh₂ deywṓs me gʷʰnih₁ént. misdʰóm moy dh₃dʰí.
Gloss: if/when-CONJ personal/2-ACC.SG.ENCL deceive-SBJV.1SG god-NOM.PL personal/1-ACC.SG.ENCL be.striking.down-OPT.3PL reward-ACC.SG personal/1-DAT.SG.ENCL give-IMP.2SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
ḱóymoy gʰóstis h₁ésti. h₁n̥gʷním ǵʰuHéye.

English: He is a guest in the household. Call upon Fire.
Gloss: village-LOC.SG guest-NOM.SG be-PRS.3SG fire.(animate-ACC.SG call-IMP.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Winter is the time of cold. What comes from the sky in winter?

PIE: ǵʰéymn̥ sríHǵesos déh₂itis h₁ésti. kʷíd ǵʰiméni diwés gʷémt?
Gloss: winter-NOM.SG cold-GEN.SG division-NOM.SG be-PRS.3SG interrogative_kwi-NOM.SG winter-LOC.SG sky-ABL.SG step-AOR.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu gʰóstis wéwket.

English: Then the guest said:
Gloss: NU guest-NOM.SG say-AOR.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
sóh₂wl̥ h₂éǵrons h₁éwset. déh₂nuh₂ térst gʷówes-kʷe tr̥sént.

English: The Sun burned the fields. The rivers dried up, and the cattle became thirsty.
Gloss: sun-NOM.SG field-ACC.PL burn-PST.3SG river-NOM.PL dry.up-AOR.3SG cattle-NOM.PL=and dry.up-AOR.3PL
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₁ésti sóḱr̥ péḱos.

English: Dung is wealth.
Gloss: be-PRS.3SG dung-NOM.SG wealth~-NOM.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Man, who are you?

PIE: kʷís h₂nér h₁ési?
Gloss: interrogative_kwi-NOM.SG man-VOC.SG be-PRS.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
I fear Father Sky.

PIE: dyḗm ph₂térm̥ bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e.
Gloss: sky-ACC.SG father-ACC.SG tremble-PRF.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Whoever hits the mouth of a husband's brother, then let him give three rams. Whoever splits the jaw of a brother-in-law, then let him leave the village.

PIE: h₁yós dayh₂urés h₁óh₃s stunédeti nu tríns moysóns h₁opéyetu. h₁yós swēḱurósyo ǵénum bʰinédeti nu só ḱóymom linékʷtu.
Gloss: relative_yo-NOM.SG brother-in-law-GEN.SG mouth-ACC.SG be.pushing-SBJV.3SG NU numerals/3-ACC.PL ram.(a.male.sheep-ACC.PL make.reach-IMP.3SG relative_yo-NOM.SG brother-in-law-GEN.SG cheek-ACC.SG be.splitting-SBJV.3SG NU demonstrative_so-NOM.SG village-ACC.SG be.leaving-IMP.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Who are you?

PIE: kʷís h₁ési?
Gloss: interrogative_kwi-NOM.SG be-PRS.2SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
swésōr sédyet.

English: The sister was sitting.
Gloss: sister-NOM.SG be.sitting-PST.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
He struck them down. They fell down, and he gave them punishment.

PIE: nu gʷʰént tóns. nu sn̥gʷént tóy ní h₁opéyet-kʷe tóybʰos kʷoynéh₂m.
Gloss: NU be.striking.down-PST.3SG demonstrative_so-ACC.PL NU fall.down-AOR.3PL demonstrative_so-NOM.PL down make.reach-PST.3SG=and demonstrative_so-DAT.PL payment-ACC.SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₁yós gʷṓs h₂isḱḗti só tód pér gʷémtu.

English: Whoever seeks the cattle, let him come through it!
Gloss: relative_yo-NOM.SG cattle-ACC.PL be.seeking-SBJV.3SG demonstrative_so-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG through step-IMP.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Ask a new question!

PIE: néwom preḱnóm préḱsdʰi.
Gloss: new-ACC.SG question-ACC.SG ask-IMP.2SG
Notes: preḱnóm: a modern coinage built from inherited roots.
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Whoever guards sheep, if a wolf devours a ram, let him not bring a ram. Whoever milks the sheep of a daughter-in-law, then let him pay two rams.

PIE: h₁yós h₂ówins péh₂seti h₁yód wĺ̥kʷos moysóm gʷr̥h₃ḗti moysóm mē wédʰet. h₁yós snusósyo h₂ówins h₂mélǵeti nu dwóh₁ moysóh₁ kʷéyetu.
Gloss: relative_yo-NOM.SG sheep-ACC.PL guard-SBJV.3SG if/when-CONJ wolf-NOM.SG ram.(a.male.sheep-ACC.SG swallow-SBJV.3SG ram.(a.male.sheep-ACC.SG NEG lead-INJ.3SG relative_yo-NOM.SG daughter-in-law-GEN.SG sheep-ACC.PL milk-SBJV.3SG NU numerals/2-ACC.DU ram.(a.male.sheep-ACC.DU pay~-IMP.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The men have thrown it. What shall I do?

PIE: h₂néres Hih₁ként. kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁oh₂?
Gloss: man-NOM.PL throw-AOR.3PL interrogative_kwi-ACC.SG be.putting-SBJV.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Then he gave them ten cattle.

PIE: nu só tóybʰos déḱm̥ gʷṓs dédeh₃t.
Gloss: NU demonstrative_so-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-DAT.PL numerals/indeclinable/10-ACC.PL cattle-ACC.PL be.giving-PST.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
She said to him:

PIE: séh₂ tósmey h₂éǵt.
Gloss: demonstrative_so-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-DAT.SG say-AOR.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu só h₁ésmey h₁éḱwom dédeh₃tu.

English: Let him give him a stallion.
Gloss: NU demonstrative_so-NOM.SG anaphoric_i-DAT.SG stallion-ACC.SG be.giving-IMP.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
méne gʷṓs h₁éḱwons-kʷe ne h₁l̥h₂ént.

English: They did not drive off my cattle and horses.
Gloss: personal/1-GEN.SG cattle-ACC.PL stallion-ACC.PL=and NEG drive.(somewhere)-AOR.3PL
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
It is the spring.

PIE: h₁ésti tód bʰréh₁wr̥.
Gloss: be-PRS.3SG demonstrative_so-NOM.SG well-NOM.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
You have freed my daughter! Protect men!

PIE: méne dʰugh₂térm̥ spr̥tóm. wiHróns h₂léksetom.
Gloss: personal/1-GEN.SG daughter-ACC.SG free-AOR.2DU man-ACC.PL be.protecting-IMP.2DU
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
A mortal made the oath before the king:

PIE: nu dʰéh₁t mórtos bʰoydʰéh₂m h₃rḗǵi.
Gloss: NU have.put-AOR.3SG mortal-NOM.SG pledge-ACC.SG king-LOC.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Call the daughter, mother!

PIE: géwHe méh₂ter dʰugh₂térm̥.
Gloss: call~-IMP.2SG mother-VOC.SG daughter-ACC.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Mother, I am thirsty.

PIE: méh₂ter tr̥syóh₂.
Gloss: mother-VOC.SG be.thirsty-PRS.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The sheep trembled. They arrived at the she-wolf and said to her:

PIE: moysṓs tr̥mént. h₁ludʰónt wl̥kʷíh₂m̥ h₂ǵént-kʷe tósyeh₂ey.
Gloss: ram.(a.male.sheep-NOM.PL be.trembling-PST.3PL arrive-AOR.3PL she-wolf-ACC.SG say-AOR.3PL=and demonstrative_so-DAT.SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
In the sky they dwell. Are they many?

PIE: dyéwi tḱiyénti. polh₁éwes h₁sénti?
Gloss: sky-LOC.SG settle-PRS.3PL much-NOM.PL be-PRS.3PL
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
dyéw moy ph₂ter séǵʰos déh₃s.

English: Father Sky, you gave me power!
Gloss: sky-VOC.SG personal/1-DAT.SG.ENCL father-VOC.SG overpowering-ACC.SG give-AOR.2SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
só tód wérǵom réh₁dʰt.

English: He carried out the work successfully.
Gloss: demonstrative_so-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG work-ACC.SG carry.out.successfully-AOR.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Strong One, I will step against you. The High One lifted up his two hands:

PIE: ḱúh₁re h₁eǵóh₂ twé próti gʷémoh₂. bʰérǵʰonts dwóh₁ ǵʰóstoh₁ úd tl̥néh₂t.
Gloss: strong-VOC.SG personal/1-NOM.SG personal/2-ACC.SG towards step-SBJV.1SG high-NOM.SG numerals/2-ACC.DU hand-ACC.DU upwards be.lifting-PST.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Mother, I shall go to the battle.

PIE: méh₂ter tóm kéh₃tum gʷéh₂oh₂.
Gloss: mother-VOC.SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG fight-ACC.SG go-SBJV.1SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₂néres tód widóyh₁ent tósyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ memnih₁ént.

English: May men see it, and may they remember his name!
Gloss: man-NOM.PL demonstrative_so-ACC.SG see-OPT.3PL demonstrative_so-GEN.SG=and name-ACC.SG think-OPT.3PL
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The two brothers made the oath.

PIE: nu bʰréh₂terh₁e bʰoydʰéh₂m dʰh₁tā́m.
Gloss: NU brother-NOM.DU pledge-ACC.SG have.put-AOR.3DU
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
They did not come near him, and they were trembling. Then an eagle stepped up and sat down upon his head.

PIE: tóm ne dʰgʷʰh₂ént trésont-kʷe. nu h₃érō gʷémt tósyo-kʷe kapwéti h₁épi sédt.
Gloss: demonstrative_so-ACC.SG NEG come.near:.almost.reach-AOR.3PL tremble.in.fear-PST.3PL=and NU eagle-NOM.SG step-AOR.3SG demonstrative_so-GEN.SG=and head-LOC.SG on sit.down-AOR.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₁yód gʷíh₃wōh₂ h₂ew gʷm̥sḱṓh₂. h₁yód séngʷoh₂ tósyeh₂ey méne h₁nómn̥ mluHdʰí.

English: If I live, I shall come again. If I fall, say my name to her.
Gloss: if/when-CONJ live-SBJV.1SG away.from be.walking-SBJV.1SG if/when-CONJ fall.down-SBJV.1SG demonstrative_so-DAT.SG personal/1-GEN.SG name-ACC.SG say-IMP.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
I stole it.

PIE: nu h₁ím stéh₂yom.
Gloss: NU anaphoric_i-ACC.SG steal-PST.1SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
bʰérǵʰew moy ǵʰóstos h₁ln̥gʷʰrós ne h₁ésti.

English: Lofty One, my hand is not lightweight.
Gloss: high-VOC.SG personal/1-GEN.SG.ENCL hand-NOM.SG lightweight-NOM.SG NEG be-PRS.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Moon, drink the water of the spring!

PIE: lówksna bʰr̥h₁wéns wódr̥ ph₃dʰí.
Gloss: moon-VOC.SG well-GEN.SG water-ACC.SG drink-IMP.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
I shall ask my brother. If he asks me for cattle, what shall I give him?

PIE: méne bʰréh₂term̥ h₁réh₁oh₂. h₁yód me h₁éy gʷṓs h₁réh₁eti kʷíd h₁ésmey h₁áyoh₂?
Gloss: personal/1-GEN.SG brother-ACC.SG ask-SBJV.1SG if/when-CONJ personal/1-ACC.SG.ENCL anaphoric_i-NOM.SG cattle-ACC.PL ask-SBJV.3SG interrogative_kwi-ACC.SG anaphoric_i-DAT.SG give.(active)-SBJV.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Then she became joyful, and her water became washed. The fish swim in her water.

PIE: nu méwdt h₁íh₂ h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe h₂ékʷeh₂ nigʷtéh₂ bʰúHt. péyskes h₁ésyeh₂s h₂ékʷeh₂i sn̥h₂énti.
Gloss: NU become.joyful-AOR.3SG anaphoric_i-NOM.SG anaphoric_i-GEN.SG=and water-NOM.SG washed-NOM.SG become-AOR.3SG fish-NOM.PL anaphoric_i-GEN.SG water-LOC.SG swim-PRS.3PL
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The hero said to the thief:

PIE: nu só wiHrós tósmey bʰréy mléwHt.
Gloss: NU demonstrative_so-NOM.SG man-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-DAT.SG thief-DAT.SG say-PST.3SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Let no one give anything. Let us build the stall again together.

PIE: nu kʷid mē h₁opéyet. nu h₁ím h₂ew ḱóm démōmes.
Gloss: NU indefinite_kwi-ACC.SG NEG make.reach-INJ.3SG NU anaphoric_i-ACC.SG away.from with build-SBJV.1PL
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
How did you come?

PIE: kʷíh₁ h₁ludʰés?
Gloss: how? arrive-AOR.2SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
They were asleep.

PIE: suptṓs h₁sént.
Gloss: asleep-NOM.PL be-PST.3PL
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
h₁yód bʰréh₂terh₁e dʰéh₁mn̥ kʷrinéh₂etes nu déḱm̥ moysóns kʷéyetām. h₁yós wósn̥ ne h₁áyeti tóm ne lémbʰeti.

English: If two brothers buy a house, then let them pay ten rams. Whoever does not give the price, he shall not seize it.
Gloss: if/when-CONJ brother-NOM.DU that.which.is.established-ACC.SG buy-SBJV.3DU NU numerals/indeclinable/10-ACC.PL ram.(a.male.sheep-ACC.PL pay~-IMP.3DU relative_yo-NOM.SG sale-ACC.SG NEG give.(active)-SBJV.3SG demonstrative_so-ACC.SG NEG seize-SBJV.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu tósyo wékʷos dʰrówgʰos.

English: His word is a lie.
Gloss: NU demonstrative_so-GEN.SG word-NOM.SG lie-NOM.SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
stnéh₂t táwros dréwi Hn̥dʰí nu h₂éwis tósmi sédt mléwHt-kʷe. táwre me dedórḱth₂e? h₂epó léytoh₂?

English: An aurochs stood under a tree. A bird sat down on him and said: "Aurochs, do you see me? Shall I go away?
Gloss: place-PST.3SG wild.bull-NOM.SG tree-LOC.SG under NU bird-NOM.SG demonstrative_so-LOC.SG sit.down-AOR.3SG say-PST.3SG=and wild.bull-VOC.SG personal/1-ACC.SG.ENCL see-PRF.2SG off go.(away)-SBJV.1SG
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
Woman, do not become afraid! I shall protect you and the sheep.

PIE: gʷḗn mē bʰéyh₂s. twé h₂ówins-kʷe h₂léksōh₂.
Gloss: woman-VOC.SG NEG become.afraid-INJ.2SG personal/2-ACC.SG sheep-ACC.PL=and be.protecting-SBJV.1SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu stéh₂dʰh₁om ḱóm h₁élh₂owos. h₁yód h₁óynos bʰéwgeti h₁énos h₁ím h₁pyéh₁t.

English: Together we shall drive the herd. If one flees, let that one seize him.
Gloss: NU herd-ACC.SG with drive.(somewhere)-SBJV.1DU if/when-CONJ one-NOM.SG flee-SBJV.3SG deictic_eno-NOM.SG anaphoric_i-ACC.SG grasp-OPT.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
nu moysós léytt wl̥kʷíh₂s-kʷe légʰyet tr̥syét-kʷe.

English: Then the ram went away, and the she-wolf lay and thirsted.
Gloss: NU ram.(a.male.sheep-NOM.SG go.(away)-AOR.3SG she-wolf-NOM.SG=and be.lying.down-PST.3SG be.thirsty-PST.3SG=and
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
wiHrṓs h₁íd kú h₂wisént?

English: Where do men hear it?
Gloss: man-NOM.PL anaphoric_i-ACC.SG where? hear-AOR.3PL
Translate English into Proto-Indo-European. Give the PIE, then a word-by-word gloss.
The man came to the great river.

PIE: nu wiHrós méǵh₂ déh₂nu h₁ludʰét.
Gloss: NU man-NOM.SG big-ACC.SG river-ACC.SG arrive-AOR.3SG
Translate Proto-Indo-European into English. Give the English, then a word-by-word gloss.
